intro.data: Now stretch the idea over a longer ladder: four tiers, Bronze ≤ Silver ≤ Gold ≤ Platinum. The fingerprint Hom(−, X) is the exact set of tiers that map INTO X — and in a ranking that's everything at or below X, no more, no less. Match each tier to its precise fingerprint. Two profiles in the right column can never happen in a ranking — leave both unpaired.
intro.alchemy: Stretch the idea over a longer ladder: four grades, Tin ≤ Bronze ≤ Silver ≤ Gold. The fingerprint Hom(−, X) is the exact set of grades that flow INTO X — everything at or below X. Match each grade to its fingerprint. Two profiles can never happen in a ranking — leave both unpaired.
intro.spellcraft: Stretch the idea over a longer ladder: four ranks, Novice ≤ Adept ≤ Master ≤ Grandmaster. The fingerprint Hom(−, X) is the exact set of ranks whose workings reach INTO X — everything at or below X. Match each rank to its fingerprint. Two profiles can never happen in a ranking — leave both unpaired.
intro.abstract: In the chain A ≤ B ≤ C ≤ D, the representable Hom(−, X) is the set of arrows into X — exactly the objects ≤ X. Match each object to its Hom(−, X). Two offered profiles are not realizable in any chain (distractors).

afterSuccess.data: You sorted four tiers using nothing but the arrows into each one, and each fingerprint was a clean run from the bottom with no gaps. Platinum is 'everything maps in'; Bronze is 'only itself maps in'. The two impostors both broke the same rule: in a ranking, if a higher tier maps into X then every lower tier does too, so Hom(−, X) can never skip a tier or skip the bottom. That gapless profile — Hom(−, X), every arrow into X — is the REPRESENTABLE functor, and it names exactly one tier.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You sorted four grades using only the processes into each, and each fingerprint was a gapless run from the bottom. The two impostors skipped grades — impossible, since a higher grade flowing in forces all the lower ones. That profile, Hom(−, X), is the representable functor; it names exactly one grade.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You sorted four ranks using only the workings into each, and each fingerprint was a gapless run from the bottom. The two impostors skipped ranks — impossible, since a higher rank reaching in forces all the lower ones. That profile, Hom(−, X), is the representable functor; it names exactly one rank.
afterSuccess.abstract: Each object X is identified by Hom(−, X), the set of arrows into it. In a chain, Hom(−, X) is the downward-closed initial segment {Y : Y ≤ X} — never a profile with a gap ({A→, C→, not B→}) or a missing least element ({B→, not A→}). Distinct objects have distinct hom-sets-of-incoming-arrows; the two non-realizable profiles name nothing.

reveal.summary: The representable functor Hom(−, X) records every arrow into X. Along a chain it is the gapless initial segment of objects ≤ X, so it pins down each object and forbids any skip-a-rank profile. An object is known by the arrows into it — the idea the Yoneda lemma makes exact.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: A value identified by its full set of constructors — and in a layered build, a layer's constructors always include every layer beneath it, never skipping one.
